Subject: Deployment packaging: conversion credits and split-ops proposal

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for taking time on the call today. As promised, attaching a draft SOW and a simple network diagram that shows where the Private (VPC) control plane and the on‑prem inference nodes sit. High level of what we folded into this draft: 

- Platform fee is presented as an annualized tier with an option to amortize over 36 months.
- We built in a one‑time conversion credit to offset overlap with your current vendor (applies for up to 24 months of committed spend).
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours, 12x5), Enhanced (24x7 + oncall rotation), and Enterprise (named SRE + monthly review). The draft tags expected response times and estimated SRE hours for each.

Key asks for Medicentra to confirm: committed annual GPU hours for Year 1 (we used your estimate of 28k) and whether you'd prefer amortized platform fee vs. up‑front invoice. Once you confirm, we will update the SOW and produce a DocuSign packet.

Attachment: Medicentra_SOW_v1.2.pdf (SOW with conversion credit table)
Attachment: network_arch_diagram_v3.png

Next steps: can we get confirmation on the GPU hours and whether procurement needs a PO prior to DocuSign? If so, we can produce a version with an invoice schedule that aligns to your PO cadence.

Best,

Hannah —

Appreciate the materials and the clear breakdown. A couple of clarifying questions before we loop procurement: 

1) The conversion credit table looks like it scales with committed spend. Can you confirm whether the credit applies to platform fee only or also to per‑token inference charges? We need to understand total economic impact.

2) For the amortization option: if we choose 36 months amortization and we terminate early (for example, after 18 months), how is the remaining platform fee handled? Any early‑termination recoup?

3) On support tiers: what’s the expected lead time to stand up a named SRE (Enterprise)? We may need that for the onboarding timeline.

We can share our year‑one GPU hours by EOD Monday. Procurement will likely require a PO in advance of DocuSign.

Folks —

FYI: Olivia's questions below. Procurement will want a PO before DocuSign, and they want the economic scope of the credit clarified (platform fee vs per‑token). I recommend we: 

1) Confirm conversion credit applies to platform fee + committed GPU hours (i.e., amortized credit toward monthly platform invoicing) but NOT to usage tier per‑token charges. That keeps per‑token incentives intact and protects net unit economics.
2) Offer a pro‑rata early‑termination clause for amortization with a 90‑day notice window and a stepdown recoup (e.g., remaining amortized platform fee less a 20% goodwill allowance). Keeps commercial protection but looks reasonable to procurement.
3) For Enterprise SRE ramp: we can commit a named SRE in 6 weeks from DocuSign signature; we can offer a 2‑week onboarding credit (one week remote shadow + one week onsite optional) as a concession to accelerate the ramp.

If you both agree, I’ll draft a short addendum to the SOW covering these three bullets and send back to Olivia with a DocuSign link. If we want to sweeten the offer, we could propose a 10% first‑year platform fee discount in exchange for a 36‑month committed term. Thoughts?

Hannah

Subject: Updated SOW + answers on credits and termination (MED-3481)

Hi Olivia / Medicentra procurement —

Thanks again for the quick turnaround on questions. Per our internal alignment, please find a short SOW addendum and an updated SOW attached. Summary of clarifications: 

- Conversion credit: applies to the platform fee portion of the commercial construct and to the amortized credit against committed GPU‑hour invoices. It does not apply to pay‑as‑you‑go per‑token inference charges. We included a worked example on page 3 of the SOW.
- Early termination / amortization: If Medicentra elects 36‑month amortization and terminates before the 36 months, we will apply a pro‑rata reconciliation for remaining amortized platform fee, less a 20% courtesy allowance. Customer must provide 90 days written notice.
- Enterprise SRE ramp: Named SRE commitment within 6 weeks of signature. We will include a 2‑week onboarding credit (remote shadowing + optional onsite week) as a one‑time concession when signed within 30 days of this offer.

I’ve also prepared two commercial pathways in the SOW: (A) 36‑month amortization with the conversion credit and an optional 10% first‑year platform discount if Medicentra signs a 36‑month committed term within 30 days; (B) 12‑month amortization with no platform discount. Choose pathway A or B and we’ll issue a DocuSign packet aligned to your PO cadence.
